Doing so took all his power and he had to build up his energy for the perfect moment. In Nadd's tomb, he moved a magical barrier rock into the Holocron room, though he had to make two tries, the second giving it all he had, though try as he might he could't break it with his power. When he fled the Orbalisks, he was able to move the stone into place much faster to seal them, since he had a new well of painful urgency. While inside, he smacked some of the creatures with a Force strike and held them away with Force deflection and his blade, but still some latched onto him.[8]

From Reven's Holocron, he learned much in his weeks of study, more than he had before from the other teachers.[1] Though he had little skill in sorcery except for a couple of rituals he put special effort into being able to employ,[2] he duly read of spells too hard and complex for him to use, but that he duly wrote down. Most important of all, he learned of the fearful Thought Bomb, a ritual he could trigger but would never dare to use, but with which he destroyed Kaan's Brotherhood by tricking Kaan into using it. In collective focus with the other Sith Masters of the Brotherhood, there was one sorcery he dared: Bane led the unleashing of a lightning storm that consumed Ruusan's landscape with a flurry of flames and death. This ritual was much like that of the Thought Bomb, where the Sith, in this case taking all the so called Dark Lords working with Bane joined their thoughts with Bane as the focus. The rite caused dark clouds to form, winds to blow, and the sky to be riven by lightning. Bane drew the lightning into himself then, with the new power gave lines of it to the other Sith as he floated five meters upwards. Boasting that now they would kill a world, Bane directed the magic, invoking a rain of hundreds of forks of lighting as his sight glared down from on high. The storm drove the Jedi out of their encampment, but before the Sith could wipe them out, Kaan and the other Sith left the attack, desiring the fun of closer combat and fearing Bane.[1]

Bane continued to augment his body, using the Force to guide his attack and defense against the great blademaster, then later Force jumping away from Ka'seem in combat.[1] He showed he could leap ten meters when he killed some rogue Sith soldiers and getting there he ran with dark side-assisted speed to get to the battle.[8] Bane used the Force to smell poison on Githany's lips when she kissed him. He was also able to sense poisons in himself and with Revan's teachings could often cure himself by purging the toxins from his body, so long as the poison did not set in before he realized and removed it. Githany's Synox, the true attack venom, was an example of something that did get past his guard, so when he studied himself and tried to burn it out with the chill fire of Bogan, but was then so weak he could only slow the spread.The Sith could also enter a hibernation trance if he chose to. By channeling the pain and anguish of others to fuel the dark side, Bane could sustain or invigorate himself. However, Bane was still susceptible to the flaw of Dark Side based healing requiring the use of inner darkness to maintain, as shown by how while he was able to sustain himself after being poisoned by the Brotherhood of Darkness long enough to be cured by Caleb, though after supping on a battlefield's pain echos and reaching for the ghosts of the death, yet he needed to further kill to tap into the pain of three farmer children and the anguish of the father to accomplish it, which gave him the last few hours he needed to find a cure.[1] After killing a few people as he was leaving Russan, he again supped on the emotions of the dead. Furthermore, Bane had the theoretical ability to draw upon the Light Side of the Force to heal himself, such as to heal his broken arm, but refrained from ever doing so—believing that invoking the Light would be against everything the Sith stood for, as well as ultimately deny him the chance to grow though suffering.[8]

After declaring himself to be a Darth, Bane stole a ship and flew it to Lehon, using the Force to fly well for an hour past the debris around the world. Bane sensed a Rancor on his way to the temple, so he took control over it with great strain and also rooted around its memories to learn about the place he was. His sense/see Force capacity let him perceive Temple of the Elders as the loadstone of the Force it was. Bane did a mental scan of the land near the temple to make sure his blade teacher had come alone to face him, just before their deadly duel. After he fell in exhaustion and Ka'seem in stone and death, he used his Force sense to seek life underneath the rubble and found nothing. When poisoned, he used his Force powers to guide him where to drive and his prima vitae picked up some scavengers. When he came to Russan, he sensed the world's Force status as a grey mess, both sides of the Force having been unleashed so and the two sides also tainted by each others' ideology. Likewise, on the planet he was able to get a vague sense of where the Jedi were, but could not crack their Force Stealth.[1] He sensed when Zannah was drawing on the Force to trip him, but his Force sense failed to pick up Zannah approaching him a fact he wondered if owed to distraction or her hiding her presence, though before felt the emotions of both Zannah, her spite towards the Jedi since her cousins were lost and when the Sith army deserters were scared of his murderous assault. On the tombworld of Nadd, he was able to sense for hundreds of kilometers that there were trees and that the tomb was a few kilometers away. After the Thought Bomb, he sensed the danger posed by eight people and learned their backgrounds and genders from two kilometers. However, on Duxon, he only precoged a big cat attacking him when it was too late and would have perished if not for it getting confused. He saw what he needed to in the Force when he went to kill the eight Sith army deserters.[8]

He shivered when the Thought Bomb's blast wave hit him, but still reached his Force sense out again and found that every member of the Brotherhood was dead. In addition, Bane had a Force-bond with Githany (and so she received visions of him). Upon finding a girl called Rain, he determined she was strong in the Force,[1] and by this same art that Tomcat was poor in the Force, barely able to use it.[8] Bane was able to easily resist Skere Kaan's mind tricks, while the other Dark Lords in the Brotherhood were unable to do so. For his part, Bane also could compel people with the Force.[1] However, he was still in agony when the Thought Bomb washed over him, leaving his brain in pain for days and it was a strain to touch the Thought Bomb, but endured the fire and ice-like agony its surface was, though he kept his mind safe from the thoughts of the dead, which tore them up even more. On his route to Nadd's tomb, he seemed haunted by Quordis's ghost, until he blasted out dark side power to dispel the ghost, though this broke the controls of his ship. He was forced to use the dark side to control the engines, his first effort only earning him a shower of sparks, but the second attempt working just well enough.[8]

In Orbalisks Clad

Darth Bane began to test his new powers almost as soon as he became bitten by the creatures at Nadd's tomb. He used the Force to study the bugs and felt physically faster and more perceptive, his healing the greater by the parisites, and more connected to the power of the Force and also balanced with the risk of losing control of his powers. By the time he was parted from his suit, he said his sheer amount of power made it easy for Jedi to sense him. He also used a pulse of the dark side to awaken Nadd's holocron. With this new power from the Orbalisks, he made a Force burst to rid himself of the seeming ghosts of Kaan and Qordis who had haunted him. When he was ambushed on Ambria in 990 BBY, the Sith assassins were able to dull his perceptions, but he noticed just in time and with a burst of red light, dispelled their arts and illusions of hiding. He also burst Farfala's stasis field after less than a second. After he got hold of Belia Darzu's holocron and slew her monster guards, he rested, then when ready used his will to turn it on and flip through it, seeking knowledge.[8]

After getting the orbalisks bonded to him, one of Bane's first acts was to fly on a drexl from Duxon to Onderon, keeping himself and his mount safe from the near lack of atmosphere by making a protective bubble around them. Soon after arriving, he intervened to save his apprentice from slavers, telekinetically tearing the saddle off a drexl and sending the crew falling to their deaths so fast he could not sup on their suffering. At the end of the battle, exerting all the power he could muster and the might he reaved by employing both consume essence and drawing upon the parisites on his body for more power, he erected a Force barrier that let him just survive a crash of three of the flying beasts that excavated a 2 meter deep and twenty wide crater, though this spent all his Force energy and most of his physical stamina. He several times had to made thousands of subatomic alterations to the items he wanted to turn into holocrons over hundreds of hours. When his fourth holocron failed, in a fit of rage he mind-flung fuel canisters fifty meters to express his anger. When a group of Shadow Assassins came at him, during the fight he make a wide attack with the Force, knocking over two, hurling a pair away, leaving only one who was able to withstand the push before Bane used his saber to slay this last one; then he flung a push at Zannah that would have broken her bones if she had not blocked it, toning its impact down to just pushing her away. On Tython, he pushed down a door after charging up his might, then soon had to use similar skills on technobeasts, at one point breaking twelve with the Force, later disintegrating two more with his powers. When the Jedi came to abolish the Sith on Tython, Bane hit Raskta Lsu with a Force wave, which would have killed the Echani woman if not for Farfala throwing a Force shield around her.[8]

In his years clad in the parisites, he continued to use lightning as well as telekinesis, burning a trio of marauders to ash and killing their winged beast with a bolt during his fight to keep Zannah from the drexl-riders. During one of his spouts of rage at failing to make a holocron, Zannah found him amid lightning-burned ground after he had burned his clothes off and made the air thick with static, so furious were his blasts of lightning. When Hetton attacked him, for once his lightning powers were cheated, when the other darksider made a Force-empowered leap away from his spray of a dozen stands. On Tython he made a wave of lightning ripple out and destroy a dozen techobeasts, much like he pulsed blue electricity when he was disarmed by the Jedi on Tython. Moments before, he shot a bolt at Farfala, blowing through the other man's Force wall, only for Lsu to save her fellow Jedi Master with her sabers.[8] At some point in the battle, he sent lightning at Sarro Xaj, only for the other human to block it on his saber, the tiny tendrils that got past seeming to do little harm.[32] His powers almost were his undoing, when he conjured a massive lightning bolt to finish off Othone, only for Worror to use his last moments of life to cage the dark power. Bane's lightning flashed around the blue shell, his azure assault bouncing around and glowing too bright to look at as he burned off his own robe and melting his specialized gear, and killed many of the animals that made his armor. Bane was thus left on the edge of death only able to live with his own endurance, his orblisks at last overtaxed.[8]

His powers of the mind continued to be potent, using the power of Beast trick to tame a drexel on Duxon and succeeding on his second attempt though it attacked him after the first, then so gaining total control over the creature. He, as before, showed the capacity to know the future, such as when he foresaw that Zannah was going to make it to Onderon (so he was able to rescue her from some slavers). On Tython, he sensed the dark side aura of Belia Darzu's fortress and that he should go to that and later he sensed Zannah and Daraovit were aboard a ship and that the other man was a weak user of the Force, but did have the Force. Much like this, he sensed the power and light of the Jedi who were coming on Zannah's heels to slay the Sith.[8]

Though he admitted he was a poor sorcerer, leaving the idea of Sith magic for Zannah after he tested her, he did attempt to create his own holocon. Besides the thousands of microscopic alterations by telekinesis he did to whenever he tried to make his own item of knowledge, he twice tried to make one with Sith sorcery glyphs but failed over the course of some months, the first time even imploding into a flash of white light. Eight years after he claimed the rank of leader of the Sith, he learned the symbols needed to be personal but on his third effort took two weeks, too long. Bane crushed the failure in his bare hands. Another, he attempted to make two years later, but once more failed and after three days and nights, was so tired he lost control to the parisites and his powers blew up the item by mistake. He also resolved to study Belia Darzu's teachings on Force alchemy.[8]

His physical prowess and combat skill was guided by the dark side to kill the last four of the Shadow Assassins who were led to him as part of Zannah's plan to get him a holocon template, then went into a Force rage when he thought Zannah had turned on him and after killing the newcomers, sunk deeper into anger and nearly slew her in his furious attack. During this fight he leapt at his student, his jump boosted by the Force, a move he also used to get next to and kill Worror. On Tython, he could have called on Bogan to destroy the technobeast virus (though the chemicals in his parasites worked to protect him so well he did not need to) and used the dark side to reduce his tiredness. When his lightning barrage got caged in with him he lived for four days with his power in the Force before a proper healer could be coerced to help him. When he tried to get Zannah to kill him on Ambria, his eyes glowed with his dark power with the intensity of his demands.[8]

Dark Lord

By 990 BBY, Bane had amassed an enormous amount of strength in the Force, viewing his power as nearly infinite and well above needing to bother with using props like Sith amulets. When he tapped into the dark side power that suffused Andeddu's Keep on Prakith, Darth Bane projected a death field that darkened the air around him and instantaneously desiccated and killed the attacking Malevolence cultists who had been unable to avoid it, aging their bodies a thousand years in a moment. This technique was extremely taxing however, and would have rapidly exhausted Bane if hadn't replenished it by feeding on the dark side, draining energies from those caught in it. While the Huntress was able to bring him down with a poisoned sword, during his resultant captivity, once Lucia gave him a cure for the poison in him, he used his powers of flame to burn out most of the lingering bad effects and now that he had been subjected and so forcibly educated in it, Bane could also destroy Senflax.[2]

By 990 BBY, Bane was able to cast electric voltage so strong that most opponents died instantly upon contact, the energy output leaving their bodies burned and charred.[2]

On Prakith, he killed several dark side cultists with Force chokes as he advanced. He was able to plunge deep into his hate and draw fully on the power of the dark side to unleash powerful Force waves, the strength of which devastated almost anything in their path.[2]

Bane owned and had access to a vast collection of Sith scrolls, tomes, and texts. With the help of individuals like Argel Tenn, he was able to obtain ancient Sith manuscripts and artifacts.[2] He got the the instructions for the creation of a holocron of his own. The Sith sorcery he learned from Nadd's holocron was admittedly beyond the scope of Bane's abilities,[8] although the stolen ritual of essence transfer from Andeddu's device was well within. Bane's own construction, created some point before 980 BBY, was a small, pyramid-shaped device that contained all of his knowledge, which he planned to pass down to future Dark Lords in his Sith Order. The gatekeeper for Bane's holocron was his own orbalisk-clad likeness.[2] His initial attempts to create a holocron ended in failure, which Bane came to believe was due to his orbalisk armor; it provided him with great power in battle, but he believed that it robbed him of the ability to use his powers for more subtle tasks. He eventually discovered that he was simply skipping a critical step in the holocron's creation out of ignorance, and later rectified his mistake.[8] Another dark trick he had was imprinting his presence on a place, so that someone hunting him with the Force would sense that spot instead of his true location.[2]

He was deeply attuned to the currents of light and dark, when great secrets could be teased out of the galaxy and he could sometimes thusly divine the will of the Force. The Dark Lord was able to Force sense a rainfall, detecting every drop and using the Force to improve his Form Three talents so that he could dodge and parry all the storm for ten minutes.[2]

Bane could keep on calling on the dark side to empower his body. On Prakith, he employed the art of enhance attribute to gain the strength to manually rip a metal hatch off.[2]

At some point, he saw a vision of Coruscant under Sith rule, something that would not come to be for hundreds of years.[20] He was deeply attuned to the currents of light and dark, when great secrets could be teased out of the galaxy and he could sometimes thusly divine the will of the Force. His Force sense was keen enough to sense every drop in a deluge while he used the Force to augment his skill in Form Three to hold off the rainfall for ten minutes. His prima vitae revealed to him where the Malevolence cultists were scurrying around him in their fortress on Prakith, there being nearly a hundred. He also sensed the power of the dark side clerics and knew that none of them could withstand him alone, but if they fought together, they might be able to defeat him.[2]

Bane was highly resistant to poison, and escaped death by its means on several occasions.[1] Serra noted while torturing him that the drugs had surprisingly little impact on him.[2]

He also possessed remarkable willpower and determination. He was able to force Andeddu's holocron to reveal to him knowledge that the holocron's gatekeeper was actively attempting to keep from him, and was skilled enough to attempt the deadly ritual of essence transfer.[2]

Other skills

As Dessel, he was a canny gambler and used insults to prod people to make bad game choices. The future Dark Lord was able to read his opponents and conceal his own feelings, talents which he used to become a talented sabacc player. Bane was a master of deception, and used his skills to fool others even before he received formal training. When he became a Sith army footsoldier, he survived at least a dozen battles in a year and became a sergeant. As a Sith trooper, he took the lives of hundreds or thousands of Republic soldiers. Early in his Sith training, he leapt up ten meters and could run five kilometers. Sometimes he could refuse to fall to insults. Bane was able to convince Githany to join him against Sirak, though he failed to bring her over to his Rule of Two ideology. Bane had scientific knowledge, enough to know the difference between male and female Rancors. He could give massages to help people feel better. Though, he endured a life of hard mining, being a soldier, Sith study and privation, and even keep driving through his poisoning to butcher his way to a cure. On Russan, he kicked another Sith's skull in, ending the mortally wounded man's life. He could put on an act like the best dramatist of Alderaan which let him make Kaan think the leader had subdued him with his mental influence.[1]

Bane could break a Neek's neck with ease and displayed a great tolerance for physical pain, such as that brought on by the orbalisk armor he was forced to wear. After being wounded almost unto death by his own rebounded lightning storm, he barely held on for four days before healing, then he was too weak to use the Force or to do more than say two words and slept for two more. When imploring Zannah to kill him, he was able to sit up. On her ship, he grappled her and could have crushed her neck, until she explained she was a proper Sith and had deceived the Jedi. Still, it was said that he would have to rest for weeks or months before he could move properly.[8]

The Dark Lord was able to use the infestation to his benefit by taking the pain and fueling his dark side rage with it. Besides being impenetrable to lightsabers, the orbalisks also provided Bane with chemical enhancements to his senses, stamina, strength, and speed. In the armor, he got back up after a drexl knocked him over, withstood force pike charges that together could have laid low a bantha, and lived through being smacked by a rancor. Furthermore, it provided him with an enhanced healing factor; a knife wound that Bane once inflicted upon himself, for instance, healed virtually as he made it, the Technobeast virus had not chance against the black bugs chemicals in Bane, and even a debilitating lightsaber strike to his arm from Johun Othone healed within seconds. Most importantly, Bane could tap into the parasites' ability to draw on the dark side to greatly increase his own power while they remained attached to him. One drawback to being infested with the orbalisks was that, because they drew on Bane's power to feed themselves, he was only capable of performing delicate tasks with the Force for a somewhat limited period of time. This was due to the fact that, in order to precisely modulate his powers for subtle tasks, he had to cut the orbalisks completely off from the dark side. This in turn caused the parasites to pump increasingly greater amounts of mood-altering chemicals into Bane's body in an attempt to get him to draw more strongly on the dark side, and thus feed them. Bane was capable of resisting the effects of the chemicals, including ever-mounting levels of pain, for a significant period of time. However, he was not immune to them, and at one point considered ridding himself of the parasites due to this problem. Ultimately, he discovered that the orbalisks did not cause nearly as great an issue with his abilities as he had feared and resolved to keep them.[8]

In his last days, Bane sometimes felt a clash between his physical might such as how he kicked the covers off his bed, left a clear dent when he hit a table, and trained strenuously; and his age, exacerbated and prematurely deepened by the suit he had worn and the constant dark energies his pulled through his body and meditated upon. His frequent hand tremor was just the most obvious of the physical ailments he had, an issue he could not cure. He was rendered slower and weaker at rest or practice than he had been, to the point that his muscles groaned and joints clicked when he did Form V lightsaber training. He even considered just going back to bed once instead of training in the rain, but the Sith pushed on and completed the set. On Prakith, he was able to wrench a tomb cover open and yank out Andeddu's holocron. In addition to his athletic skills, he was a skilled pilot who made hundreds of hyperspace jumps as he sought for Darth Andeddu's holocron and landed his ship safely. The Sith was not invulnerable, of course, being staggered and stunned by a sonic attack during the raid on his house on Ciutric IV and during the furious battle, though he unleashed his powers--even punching through his powers being partly suppressed--he got blinded and pushed back by flash gernades and kicked over a banister. Though he recovered his dropped saber and slashed down two men, the Huntress was able to cut him with her sword and as he dodged blaster bolts and chased the other Force user, he passed out from the poison hidden on the Iktotchi woman's weapon. When Serra tortured him, he went through ten seconds and then almost twice that in poison seizures that made him dreary and almost unable to talk. With a bit of help, he was able to recover and use his powers to shatter his chains with his will and then break out, killing two men with his hands, knifing a woman, and gunning down two more guards whose shots he dodged. After all this effort, he still was able to bodyslam his way though a door. In his last battle, his unarmed strikes broke Zannah's bones and he kept on fighting even after a dark side tendril struck off part of his shoulder and filled him with the dread of absolute annihilation, the cold horror of the void itself.[2]

Underpinning his deeds was a deep intelligence. Bane determined that a newway of Sith practice, his Rule of Two, needed to be exalted to replace the Brotherhood of Darkness.[1] He was a very skilled teacher in the dark side, using insults and yelling along with philosophy and encouragement to train Zannah to become a Sith. He also was a crafty planner, he made sure to make dossiers on the various Jedi who might be a threat to him and exploited their lack of central authority and control to slip Zannah into the Jedi Temple, pretending to be a random Jedi Padawan. By the time of his near death at his own hand, he had a hundred political plans set in motion. The Sith noticed at a glance that Hetton was not learned in the use of his green lightsaber and Bane was trained in first aid.[8] Considered by his student to be a master manipulator, he set up a bunch of political plots up, such as his informants in the Desilijic Hutt clan and some of his investments repaid themselves a hundred times over. Bane also developed more self-control in the decade after he was forced to shed his armor, his agressive instinct where he might have blindly charged in was tempered by the time he went after Andeddu's pyramid of knowledge. He also made sure to learn the name and reputation of every Jedi Master. A canny debater, he almost got Serra to agree that he was in the right, even as she was torturing him for killing her father. Almost a thousand years after he fell, the path he saw and set Zannah on would bear fruit,[2] with the Jedi being smashed and a Sith Lord rising to rule the galaxy as Emperor.[25]

Darth Bane was an author, writing about Sith ideology and training in his essay The Rule of Two, a seminal work that Palpatine included in his own textbook on the dark side. Though, in this, Bane did make[20] a slight error in the genetic relation between his student and her kinsman.[8][20]

Equipment

During his time in the Gloom Walkers unit, Dessel used a TC-22 blaster rifle. He became skilled in the use of the weapon, and chose to stick with the first blaster he learned to use instead of switching to a different weapon. As a sergeant, Dessel was allowed to wield a secondary weapon, and so carried an advanced GSI-21D pistol, able to disintegrate armor. He also kept a vibroblade in his boot. Upon entry into the Sith Academy, Bane was trained in lightsaber combat with durasteel training sabers that were covered in the poisonous barbs of the pelko bug. Later, his blade mentor presented him with a hook-handle lightsaber, that would remain his sword. On Russan, he wore the Sith armor his people were expected to be clad in.[1]

For a time, Bane flew the starship Valcyn, a T-class long-range personal cruiser that had originally belonged to Qordis. After he returned from the tombs on Korriban in an effort to find knowledge, Bane declared his abandonment of the Brotherhood, and aware that Qordis would not try to stop him, left the planet in the Headmaster's ship. Bane traveled to Lehon, Ambria, and Ruusan in the highly advanced ship before he crashed on Dxun.[1][8] By 980 BBY, the Dark Lord had come to own a Theta-class T-1 vessel named the Triumph. The Cygnus Spaceworks vessel could be flown by one pilot, which Bane used to his advantage in 980 BBY when he made a trip to the Deep Core planet Prakith without informing his apprentice. His return trip to his mansion on Ciutric IV proved to be Bane's final journey in his shuttle, as he was ambushed on the planet and taken to Doan.[2]

Behind the scenes

Character origins

"One of the themes throughout the films is that the Sith lords, when they started out thousands of years ago, embraced the dark side. They were greedy and self-centered and they all wanted to take over, so they killed each other. Eventually, there was only one left, and that one took on an apprentice. And for thousands of years, the master would teach the apprentice, the master would die, the apprentice would then teach another apprentice, become the master, and so on. But there could never be any more than two of them, because if there were, they would try to get rid of the leader, which is exactly what Vader was trying to do, and that's exactly what the Emperor was trying to do. The Emperor was trying to get rid of Vader, and Vader was trying to get rid of the Emperor."
―George Lucas[33]

The character of Darth Bane, and his Rule of Two, were created by George Lucas as part of his backstory of the Sith he developed for the prequel trilogy.[34] Bane was first mentioned in The Phantom Menace novelization as the creator of the Rule of Two. In 2000, The Essential Chronology collated these events with the Battle of Ruusan mentioned in Dark Forces: Jedi Knight, creating a backstory further developed in Jedi vs Sith by Darko Macan and Bane of the Sith by Kevin J. Anderson. The New Essential Guide to Characters and The New Essential Chronology provided more details, and the latter attempted to correct inconsistencies between Jedi vs Sith and Bane of the Sith.

In 2006, Darth Bane: Path of Destruction, written by Drew Karpyshyn was released. Several of the details in it contradicted previous information about Bane. Another novel about Darth Bane, Darth Bane: Rule of Two, was released in 2007 and fixed some of the conflicting elements. Part of the novel covers Bane of the Sith, while it also invents new history for Bane and his apprentice. A third novel, Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil, was released in 2009. Each of these novels expanded on Bane's backstory, with Dynasty of Evil killing off the Dark Lord.

Many fans were initially confused as to whether Bane or Zannah won the final duel between the two at the end of Dynasty of Evil. Author Drew Karpshyn confirmed a few days later that Zannah had won the duel, although a small remnant of Bane remained in her.[13]

For the Star Wars: The Clone Wars television series, Bane was to originally appear, alongside Darth Revan, in the third season episode "Ghosts of Mortis" as an influence to the Force-wielding Son, an embodiment of the dark side of the Force. Although George Lucas commissioned the scene about two ancient Sith, he later cut it before the scene could be fully animated, since it conflicted with Lucas's views on the Force. Supervising Director Dave Filoni voiced similar concerns to the inclusion of the two Sith Lords; though the scene would have been appreciated by Expanded Universe fans, he stated that cutting the scene had been the right thing to do.[35] The fact that Revan later converted to the light side could also have raised continuity issues if he did appear as a Sith spirit.[36] Darth Bane himself later appeared in the sixth season episode "Sacrifice" as an illusion that Yoda had to face. He was given a previously unseen design and voiced in the episode by Mark Hamill, the actor who played Luke Skywalker in the original trilogy.[37]

Lucasfilm official Leland Chee stated in his blog that Bane's name is based on the word "Bane,"[38] which means, among other things, "a person or thing that ruins or spoils."[39] Jan Duursema's depiction of Bane in Star Wars: Legacy was based on the partially completed costume of a fan, Thomas J. Spanos.[40]

Contradictions

Various contradictions, both major and minor, exist between sources involving Bane. In both the short story Bane of the Sith and Bane's biography in The New Essential Guide to Characters, it is implied that Bane trained exclusively beneath Qordis, while in the novel he trained under Qordis and many other Sith Masters.[1] Also, in Bane of the Sith and Path of Destruction, Bane's lightsaber hilt is clearly described as being "hooked." However, in almost every illustration, even those from after the publishing of Path of Destruction, Darth Bane is depicted with a standard-hilt lightsaber. The illustrations also frequently depict Bane wielding a purple lightsaber, though this was later corrected on the cover art of Darth Bane: Rule of Two. A picture of the curved hilt was finally included in The Essential Reader's Companion.

In Bane of the Sith, Bane escapes from Ruusan when his warning to Kaan not to use the thought bomb goes unheeded. The dark side spirits call him a coward for running, and Bane defends himself by saying that the Sith must survive. Until he gets to Onderon, he intends to resurrect the system of the Brotherhood.[41] In Path of Destruction, Bane comes to detest the Brotherhood after studying Revan's holocron and the ancient records when he realizes that the Sith can never be united or equal. He plots to destroy the Brotherhood by giving Kaan the formula for using the thought bomb and feigning to join them under the guise of wanting to take over leadership.[1]

The events of Bane of the Sith are retold in Rule of Two. In Bane of the Sith, ghosts of Kaan and Qordis appear and Bane learns that the creatures that cover him are called "orbalisks" from Qordis,[41] but Rule of Two retconned the ghosts of Kaan and Qordis into hallucinations resulting from the thought bomb damaging Bane's brain and has Bane learn about the orbalisks from Freedon Nadd's holocron.[8]

This article tends to support the details described by Path of Destruction and Rule of Two, as those are the newer sources and are followed by a sequel.

Chronologically speaking, Darth Rivan predates Darth Bane,[17] and Darth Bane is the author of the Rule of Two.[1] However, one of the traps in Darth Rivan's fortress, as shown in A Mon Alone, is based on the Sith adherence to the Rule of Two.[42]

Despite a model for Bane that was created for The Clone Wars season three episode "Ghosts of Mortis" that was consistent with his previous appearances, including his orbalisk armor, the season six episode "Sacrifice" features an apparition of Darth Bane that is much different from any of his previous appearances, wearing a suit of armor much different than any of those he had previously been seen wearing.
